claims.statement: The pinned family-332 manuscript claims that the real sequence space ℓ1 has metric Markov cotype 2 with N2(ℓ1) ≤ 12√21, uniformly over every finite number of states, every integer time t≥1, every probability vector (allowing zero entries), every reversible stochastic matrix, and every input family in ℓ1.
assumptions: Real ℓ1 with its standard metric
Finite-state reversible Markov chain as in Definition 1.1 of the release
claims.status: source-reported; independently internally reconstructed on the load-bearing proof pages; not externally validated or formalized
claims.novelty_boundary: The pinned manuscript itself reports the theorem; family-332 proof reconstruction was already recorded in Astra cycle 19. This audit claims neither authorship nor external proof validation.

costs.proof_scope: Finite-dimensional cut code has at most 2^n-2 coordinates; constant is independent of n, t, and source-coordinate count.
costs.algorithmic_cost: No efficient or finite-precision extension algorithm is supplied or claimed.

claims.falsifier: A counterexample or invalid step in the cut recovery, quartic estimate, martingale telescoping, stopped-jump weights, or geometric endpoint comparison would refute the release claim or this reconstruction.
claims.next_gate: Independent expert or formal proof validation of the pinned manuscript.

claims.statement: Conditional on MC-1, every real ambient L1(Ω,μ) has metric Markov cotype 2 with N2(L1(Ω,μ)) ≤ 12√21, for arbitrary measure spaces, without σ-finiteness assumptions.
assumptions: Finite cut operations are applied to representatives of each finite family of L1 classes
The standard weighted finite-ℓ1 rescaling and coordinate projection are used
claims.status: internally proved conditional transfer; not a claim printed in the pinned release and not externally validated
claims.proof_path: work/agents/kls_proof_audit/markov_cotype_reuse/FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Conditional transfer to every ambient real L1'
claims.novelty_boundary: This is the finite-cut transfer from ℓ1 to ambient L1; the cited 2026 metric-cotype paper gives cut methods for L1 but a different invariant. Priority remains unknown.

costs.finite_code_size: At most 2^n-2 cut coordinates for n input points.
costs.constant_loss: None: the cut map is contractive and preserves all input pairwise distances exactly.

claims.falsifier: Failure of measurability/integrability of finite cut functions, noncontractivity of recovery, or a discrepancy between weighted-ℓ1 code distances and L1 input distances.
claims.next_gate: Independent review of the conditional finite-cut transfer and release premise.

claims.statement: Conditional on MC-2, for every metric source X with finite Markov type 2 constant M2(X), every subset Z⊆X, and every Lipschitz f:Z→L1(Ω,μ;R), there is a global extension F:X→L1(Ω,μ;R) with Lip(F) ≤ C_MN·12√21·M2(X)·Lip(f), where C_MN is the universal constant hidden in Mendel–Naor's ≲. No separability assumption is required on X, Z, or the L1 target.
assumptions: MC-2 holds for the ambient target Y=L1(Ω,μ;R)
Mendel–Naor Theorem 1.11 applies to the finite metric Markov cotype target
The linear mean on the Banach target is W2-barycentric with constant 1

Globalization of MN finite extensions into Y** uses either its source-reported ultrafilter/local-reflexivity route (with Heinrich Proposition 6.7's canonical-boundary compatibility) or the direct weak*-Tychonoff finite-intersection proof in FINAL_REPORT.md
The standard norm-one L-projection from Y** onto canonical Y is used
claims.status: conditional theorem derived from MC-2 and established Banach-space extension/L-embeddedness results; not the literal statement of release Corollary 6.2; not externally validated as a consequence of the candidate release
claims.proof_path: work/agents/kls_proof_audit/markov_cotype_reuse/FINAL_REPORT.md, section 'Conditional global extension deduction, including nonseparable sources'
claims.novelty_boundary: The release prints the Hilbert-to-ℓ1 case via ℓ1=c0*. Ambient-L1 and nonseparable-source coverage is a formal deduction using the MN bidual route and L-embeddedness. Earlier cited open-problem sources predate the release; exhaustive priority search was not performed.

costs.extension_factor: Existential universal C_MN is not numerically specified in the cited theorem's ≲ notation.
costs.construction: The ultrafilter or weak*-Tychonoff compactness route and the bidual projection are nonconstructive; no algorithm, runtime, precision bound, or computable witness selector is claimed.
costs.separability: None required; the argument indexes all finite subsets of the source.

claims.falsifier: Invalidity of the finite-target extension hypotheses, a defect in the direct compactness finite-intersection construction or the source's ultrafilter route, or failure of L1 L-embeddedness for a measure-space class included in the statement.
claims.next_gate: Independent review of the MN finite-extension theorem, the direct weak*-compactness passage, and the L1 L-projection, then external validation of MC-1.

claims.statement: The bad closed-subspace example inside ℓ1 does not contradict MC-2 or MC-3, and it does not establish extension into arbitrary closed subspaces: metric Markov cotype need not pass to subspaces, while the extension witnesses constructed in the ambient target may leave a prescribed subspace.
assumptions: Mendel–Naor Theorem 1.14 as stated in their 2013 paper
The target of MC-2 and MC-3 is the full ambient L1 space
claims.status: source-reported scope limitation, checked against the definitions

claims.novelty_boundary: No claim is made about all subspaces of L1 or extension into those subspaces.
claims.falsifier: A theorem that the relevant cotype property passes to all closed subspaces, or that the extension construction remains inside the prescribed subspace, would change the scope analysis.
